title: Longest Streak of Ones
statement:
You get an array bits that holds only 0s and 1s, for example a log of days on which a build passed (1) or failed (0).

Return the length of the longest run of consecutive 1s. If there are no 1s at all, return 0.

examples.why: The runs of ones have lengths 1, 2 and 1. The total number of ones, 4, is not the answer.
The longest run ends at the last index. Updating the best only when a 0 appears would miss it.

hints: You only ever care about the run that is going on right now and the best run so far.
A 1 extends the current run; a 0 ends it.
Keep two counters, current and best. Update best after every 1, not only when a run ends.

explain.intuition:
Read the array once and keep a counter of how many ones you have seen in a row. A 1 adds to it, a 0 resets it to zero. The answer is the largest value the counter ever reaches.

The one trap is when you record that largest value. If you only record it when a 0 arrives, a run that reaches the end of the array never gets recorded. Record it after every step instead.
steps: For each bit: if it is 1, increase current and set best = max(best, current).
pitfalls: Updating best only when a zero appears, which loses a run at the end, like in [0, 1, 1, 1].
Counting all the ones instead of consecutive ones.

solutions.title: Extend from every start
solutions.idea: From each index, count how many ones follow without a break.

solutions.title: Running counter
solutions.idea: Grow a counter on 1, reset it on 0, and keep the largest value it reaches.

followups: You may flip at most one 0 into a 1. What is the longest run now? (Hint: a sliding window.)
The bits arrive as an endless stream. Can you still answer after every new bit?
